target_customer: Women with pelvic floor issues such as postpartum and incontinence, paying per visit or via subscription
problem: Pelvic floor physical therapy is hard to access and expensive; a digital platform makes it available remotely.
business_model: consumer subscription (site later showed 11.99 dollars monthly, 29.99 quarterly, 59.99 annual with a 7 day trial) after earlier per visit pricing of 100 dollars evaluation and 75 dollars follow ups reported by a directory
product_category: Digital women's health rehabilitation, pelvic floor

founders.name: Katy Honda
education: Stanford, BS Science, Technology, and Society

technical_complexity.rationale: Video visits and content programs are standard; the hard parts were licensing and clinical operations rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Telehealth and exercise apps were easy to copy and well funded rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors expanded into pelvic health (Hinge program, Sword Bloom, Origin nationwide); Comet is listed Inactive by YC though its site was still live in this session.

market_need_then: Pelvic floor care was under served and venture funded telehealth rivals were launching products in 2021, but dated sources for demand were not found.

branding.domain_note: Used trycomet.com, a try prefix domain; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Wellness and fitness positioning, programs designed by physical therapists

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community found; name collides with many Comet companies.

pivots.from: Virtual pelvic floor physical therapy visits
pivots.to: At home pelvic floor, flexibility and posture fitness programs in an iOS app
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the site contrasting with the YC description and earlier directory pricing, unverified.

outcome_analysis: Comet Health started as a virtual pelvic floor physical therapy company in Summer 2021 and the current site sells a low priced fitness app instead, while YC lists it as Inactive. No post-mortem or funding news was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty; the move toward a wellness app suggests the clinical model may not have scaled but that is unsourced.
notes: 125K funding rests on a single database listing with no date or investors. Pivot is inferred from site and directory text and is unverified. Competitor sources found were undated or later (mobihealthnews Hinge pelvic floor item undated), so the list is empty. The website was live with a 2026 copyright line, conflicting with the Inactive label.
